subject: [PATCH v3 08/11] mm, swap: only charge physical swap entries

2026-08-06.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory control group (memcg) and swap management to only charge physical swap entries, rather than charging for virtual swap entries when they are allocated. This change ensures that memory.swap.current accurately tracks on-disk swap usage, preventing overcharging of zswap-backed or zero-filled pages. As a result, cgroups with all pages in zswap can reclaim anonymous memory even if memory.swap.max is set to 0.

reviews.author: Johannes Weiner
reviews.summary:
The reviewer confirmed that the patch aligns with cgroup semantics, specifically that memory.swap.* counters track physical swap space and should be 0 when using zswap without a backing file or when only writing to the swapfile.

Reviewer Johannes Weiner requested a proper refactoring of the swap-related functions, suggesting that they be split into two separate functions: __mem_cgroup_swap_record() and __mem_cgroup_swap_charge(), to improve code organization and maintainability.

Reviewer noted that __mem_cgroup_swap_uncharge() does not drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), which can cause a lock ordering violation when reclaim paths are involved.

Reviewer Johannes Weiner suggested removing __mem_cgroup_uncharge_swap() and handling the swap put operation similarly to the charge path, specifically by calling __mem_cgroup_swap_put().

Reviewer noted that the patch introduces a potential deadlock between vswap_free() and reclaim paths due to the acquisition of the per-vswap spinlock while holding the folio lock, and requested the lock be dropped before calling try_to_unmap().

Reviewer noted that the patch does not properly handle the case where vswap is NULL, and suggested adding a check to call mem_cgroup_swap_uncharge() before calling mem_cgroup_swap_put().
reviews.raw_body:
To head off any uncertainty about this: this is exactly what needs to
happen in terms of cgroup semantics.

memory.swap.* are about physical swap space. They track, control, and
enforce fairness for a finite resource that is separate from memory.

When a user switches on vswsap and a bunch of empty pages are stored
inside the zeromap without consuming swapfile space, these counters
must be 0.

When a user switches on vswap to use zswap without a backing file,
these counters must be 0.

When a user switches on vswap to use zswap with writeback, only the
pages that get written to the swapfile must be tracked and controlled
by these counters.

A few inline comments on the implementation:

---

These functions are just __mem_cgroup_try_charge_swap() in two acts :-)

Please refactor this properly:

__mem_cgroup_swap_record()
__mem_cgroup_swap_charge()

---

Same on the uncharge side...

__mem_cgroup_swap_uncharge()

---

__mem_cgroup_swap_put()

and then remove __mem_cgroup_uncharge_swap(). Handle this split the
same way as on the charge path.

---

This becomes:

	if (!vswap && mem_cgroup_swap_try_charge())
		abort
	mem_cgroup_swap_record()

---

And this becomes:

	if (!vswap)
		mem_cgroup_swap_uncharge()
	mem_cgroup_swap_put()

2026-08-07.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory management to only charge physical swap entries when they acquire actual backing, rather than immediately upon allocation. This change ensures that memory.swap.current accurately reflects on-disk swap usage and prevents zswap-backed pages from being counted as occupying swap space. As a result, cgroups with all pages in zswap can now reclaim anonymous memory even if memory.swap.max is set to 0.
